recipes.name: Loaded Chili Sweet Potato Fries
instructions: Line two baking trays and preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C)*.
Cut the sweet potatoes into ½ inch (1 cm) thick sticks**. Transfer the potatoes to a large bowl.
Drizzle the cut potatoes with the oil and sprinkle with the cornstarch and spices.
Divide the fries over the baking trays. Spread the fries as far apart from each other as possible. Bake for 20 minutes.
Flip the fries and switch the upper and lower baking tray. Continue to bake for another 20 to 25 minutes.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. When hot, add the onion and garlic, and cook for 3 to 4 minutes.
Then add the spices. Cook for another 1 minute, stirring throughout.
Add the remaining chili ingredients. Cook at a gentle simmer, partially covered, for 20 minutes. Stir occasionally.
To make the cheese sauce, cover the cashews with boiling water and let them soak for at least 10 minutes, then drain.
Add the drained cashews and remaining sauce ingredients to a high-speed blender. Blend until smooth.
Add the blended mixture to a saucepan and heat through. Then set aside.
To make the salsa, combine the ingredients in a small food processor or chop finely and mix together in a bowl.
Assemble by placing the fries on a plate. Top with chilli.
Drizzle over the cheese sauce, salsa, and any other desired garnishes. Enjoy!

page_recipe_notes: Notes † For us, 4 medium sweet potatoes weighed about 800 g. † We use pure ground chili powder made from dried chili peppers - not to be confused with the chili powder spice blend commonly found in the US, which often includes cumin, garlic powder, and other seasonings. For the intended heat and flavour, be sure to use pure chili powder. * We used top and bottom heating (not fan-assisted/convection). ** Try to cut the fries in similar thicknesses, so they will cook evenly.
Storage Best if enjoyed immediately. The chili, cheese sauce, and salsa can be made ahead of time and stored in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days.
